newsitem.title: USA: Storm causes flooding, mudslides in California.
newsitem.headline: Storm causes flooding, mudslides in California.

text.p: The latest in a series of Pacific storms sent several northern California rivers above flood stage on Sunday while overflowing streams flooded homes and streets.

State officials anxiously watched fragile levees on large rivers as the water rose again only a few weeks after devastating floods over the New Year's holiday damaged thousands of homes and inundated huge areas of farmland, causing at least $1.5 billion of damage.

The weekend storm, the second this week, caused havoc on the state's roads. U.S. Highway 50, a key link between northern California and Nevada, was closed in the Sierra Nevada mountains after part of a hillside collapsed late on Friday night, covering a long stretch with mud and rock up to 70 feet (20 metres) deep.
Highway 101, a busy north-south route, was closed in San Jose due to flooding on Sunday.
A mudslide plowed into a home in Mill Valley, near San Francisco, and police chief Fred Lau lived in one of 10 homes evacuated in San Francisco due to a slide.
Flood-weary residents were pleased that rainfall from the latest storm was at the lower end of the three to six inch (7.5 to 15 cm) range predicted by meteorologists.
"I'm glad we came out at the shorter end of the scale," National Weather Service forecaster Dan Kearns said.
But the rain ran off onto the saturated ground, turning usually docile streams and rivers into raging brown torrents.
Heavy rain overnight caused streams to suddenly rise and overflow in Roseville and Granite Bay, two towns about 20 miles (32 kms) northeast of Sacramento, local officials said.
Thirteen homes, which were under up to six inches (15 cms) of water, were damaged in Granite Bay, said Tino Guevara, a spokesman for Placer County.
In Roseville, two homes, five garages and a number of businesses were flooded when several streams overflowed on Sunday morning, city spokeswoman Marilyn Bartell said.
The Russian and Napa rivers in northern California's wine country crested above flood stage in several places on Sunday morning, but were expected to recede later in the day.
Kearns said it was likely that some buildings in low-lying areas along the Russian River would be flooded.

Flood warnings were in effect at various points of the San Joaquin, Merced, Tuolumne and Cosumnes rivers in central California, Anita Fante, a spokeswoman for the California Department of Water Resources, said. There was severe flooding along several of those rivers earlier this month.

Fante said water officials were very concerned about the Sacramento and San Joaquin valleys, where two of the state's main rivers run. "They are all very wet. Levees can be very unpredictable," she said.

Dry weather was forecast for the rest of this week, except for showers on Tuesday, but Fante said officials would still watch rivers and levees closely. "Even when we have good weather, you can still have levee breaks," she said.
